channel.title: CTV News – Toronto City Hall
channel.description: Toronto City Hall coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Ford backs Chow’s use of strong mayor powers to replace Toronto’s city manager
A 911 fee on cellphone bills and a commercial parking levy among new revenue tools proposed for Toronto
item.description: The City of Toronto is looking for new ways to boost its cash-strapped coffers amid “current and longer-term financial pressures,” including a $1.1 billion budget shortfall next year.

item.title: Toronto’s water and solid waste rates could be going up: Here’s how much
item.description: Garbage and water costs will be going up for Toronto residents next year if city council adopts the latest rate recommendation being set forth by staff to be included in the upcoming budget.

item.title: Toronto’s top bureaucrat out as Olivia Chow seeks to ‘reorganize’ city administration
item.description: Paul Johnson is out as Toronto’s top bureaucrat after Olivia Chow used strong mayor powers to shake up the administration at city hall.

item.title: New TTC Board chair says he’s concerned about allegations surrounding CEO
item.description: Newly appointed TTC Board Chair Paul Ainslie says recent questions around the commission’s leadership and spending are “very concerning” to him and he intends to follow up on them in his new role.

item.title: Chow shakes up city hall leadership, taps former Liberal MP for housing
item.description: Mayor Olivia Chow is again turning down a post on the Toronto police board while opting to stick with the same roster of deputy mayors as when she finished her first term.

item.title: Mayor Chow lays out vision for new term, Malik elected as new speaker
item.description: Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow says she is planning to fulfill in the next four years the mandate given to her by residents: to make the city “more caring, more affordable, and safer.”

item.title: Can advocates elected to Toronto council help fix housing and homelessness crisis?
item.description: Toronto’s newly elected council includes several prominent tenant and housing rights activists and advocates for the city’s homeless population who say they will bring the kind of first-hand outreach experience to the table that council needs.

item.title: Toronto introduces hiring freeze amid $1.1B shortfall
item.description: Toronto is implementing a hiring freeze as it stares down a shortfall of $1.1 billion in its 2027 budget.

item.title: Toronto wants a new deal with the province. Doug Ford says the answer is ‘no’
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says the province will not be hammering out a so-called “New Deal 2.0” to solve Toronto’s finances.

item.title: Why Toronto's municipal election turnout beat the provincial average
item.description: What appeared to be a neck-and-neck race between two top contenders for the mayor’s seat helped draw more people to the polls in Toronto, leading to the city’s highest turnout in more than a decade, some experts say.

item.title: After election victory, Chow to face budget pressure and new deal with Ontario
item.description: Negotiations with the province to help relieve Toronto’s budget pressures loomed over Olivia Chow’s election victory, as she vowed to be the “mayor for everyone.”

item.title: Olivia Chow answered questions day after earning second term. Here’s everything she said
item.description: Olivia Chow spoke with reporters on Tuesday afternoon following a decisive win against Brad Bradford in the Toronto mayoral election.

item.title: Here’s a list of what Olivia Chow has promised to do in her second term
item.description: Olivia Chow has managed to hang on to the top job on council, fending off a challenge from Brad Bradford to keep her job. Here’s everything Chow has said she would do in her second term.

item.title: Take a closer look at some of the more closely contested Toronto city council races
item.description: Outside of the Toronto mayoral race, there were several contests for city council seats that made headlines in the leadup to Monday’s election, including four wards where an incumbent was not running.
